task.title: Ideas Draft: other code visualizations beyond the parse tree and git history
task.description:
Parking lot for visualization ideas discussed on 2026-10-09 that are not yet stories. Not for implementation as-is; pull individual items into their own stories when wanted.

From the parse tree and git history (cheap, data mostly already in the snapshot):
- Hotspots: complexity x churn scatter or treemap tint; the top-right corner is the risk.
- Blast radius: shade everything that transitively depends on a file or module; on the compare view, changed files plus their dependents as a review map.
- Co-change coupling: files that land in the same commits more than chance, as a second edge kind; the overlay of co-change edges with no import edge shows hidden coupling (e.g. across the Go/TS boundary).
- Knowledge map and bus factor: author distribution per file from git log plus mailmap; single-author regions highlighted.
- Age and fossils: last-touched date per file/line; 'recently added and already churning' filter.
- Instability/abstractness plane (Martin metrics from fan-in/fan-out in coupling[]).
- Cohesion and misplaced files: internal vs outgoing edge ratio per directory; files whose imports mostly point elsewhere.
- Reachability and orphans from entry points; unused exports (needs named-import tracking).
- Flow between top-level directories (Sankey/chord of import volume).
- Clone map via token winnowing fingerprints drawn as links on the treemap.
- Growth curves per module (stacked area over time).
- Edge age and architecture drift: first-seen commit per edge; highlight edges younger than N weeks.
- Structural changelog: generated text per compare range (functions added/removed/moved/grown, exported signature hash changes, edges added, cycles introduced, modules split/merged).
- Fitness rules over history: declarative 'nothing in core imports cli' rules evaluated per commit as a pass/fail timeline.
- Refactoring detection: file splits, extractions, move clusters via the rename map plus function-name matching.
- AI authorship: share of code per module from Co-Authored-By trailers; does agent-authored code churn differently.
- Collaboration network: who touches the same files.
- Vocabulary analysis: identifier term frequency per module; overlap without an import edge suggests duplication or a missing abstraction.
- Documentation staleness: doc/README last-touched vs adjacent code churn.
- Markers: TODO/FIXME/deprecation density with blame age.

From runtime data (needs an input artifact; mostly fits the generic overlay story):
- Coverage reports (lcov, go cover) as an overlay; per-test coverage gives a test-to-code map.
- Traces and profiles (pprof, OTel, Chrome profiles): dynamic call graph as edge weights over the static graph; static edges with no runtime traffic.
- Error tracking (Sentry, logs): exceptions per file/function as a heat layer.

From cost data:
- Bundler metafiles (esbuild/Rollup/Vite stats) and Go link maps: shipped bytes per source file next to source bytes.
- Lockfiles over time: transitive dependency graph with versions, release age, duplicates, licenses, OSV advisories; dependency churn as a view.
- CI data (GitHub Actions): build/test duration, failure rate, flaky tests mapped to modules.

From boundaries the parser cannot see (fits the extracted-boundary-edges family):
- Code to schema: migrations into a table graph, SQL strings and ORM models matched to tables; schema churn timeline.
- Configuration surface: process.env / os.Getenv / feature flag / path literal references per module.
- Queues, events, and jobs: publish/subscribe matched by topic name.
- OpenAPI, gRPC protos, GraphQL schemas as provides/consumes sources.

From people and process:
- PR metadata: review time, review rounds, comment density per file; time-to-merge over time.
- Issue/task links: bug-fix commits by linked issue or message convention give defect density per module; Workbook task keys in commit messages.

Non-deterministic but worth exploring:
- Semantic clustering: embed files, cluster, compare clusters to the directory tree; disagreement shows where folder structure drifted from what the code is about.
